sut.name: trainticket
sut.deploy: kind cluster 'mist', ns trainticket (quick_start base codewisdom/*:1.0.0); FORK ts-admin-basic-info-service:1.0.5 built from the clean a1767ab3 working tree, kind-loaded, swapped in via kubectl set image + set env MIST_FAULT_LOSTWRITE_ENABLED=true for the capture, then RESTORED to base 1.0.0 (flag env removed).

readback.locator: GET /api/v1/adminbasicservice/adminbasic/contacts [membership by business key accountId+documentNumber; NO per-entity GET on adminbasic -> collection-membership read-back]

config.site: AdminBasicInfoServiceImpl.addContact (@Value mist.fault.lostwrite.enabled, Spring relaxed binding; skips the persist POST to ts-contacts-service)
config.applied_via: kubectl set env on the deployment

negative_control.replay_script: TT-adminbasic-contacts-control-001 (SAME fork image digest, env flag false -> same-binary twin differing ONLY in the flag; closes R9)

ground_truth.label: positive
ground_truth.rationale: With the flag on, addContact returns HTTP 200 {status:1,msg:"create contacts success",data:null} but SKIPS the persist POST to ts-contacts-service, so the contact is never saved. Clean ack, lost write. Norm from the SUT contract; the absent durable row is presented via read-back: the submitted accountId+documentNumber never appears in the GET list.

provenance.notes: LIVE-CAPTURED 2026-07-10 (breadth wave): POST {id 6d1c9a4b..., documentNumber BR-FLT-R2-20260710} acked 200 {1,"create contacts success",null}; read-back ABSENT; TRIPLE corroboration incl. the pod's own log line '[addContact][INJECTED FAULT][LOST_WRITE_FAULT] acknowledging success WITHOUT persisting contact id: 6d1c9a4b...'. Second lost-write positive on a DIFFERENT write-path service (triple B; not adminroute-specific); collection-membership read-back (adminbasic has NO per-entity GET). CAPTURE-HYGIENE INCIDENT (disclosed): the first capture attempt ran during the deployment rollout and was served by the STILL-NACOS-REGISTERED terminating base pod (ack "Create Success", row persisted -> INVALID as a fault capture); the run was re-executed with FRESH ids after routing convergence (probe-first discipline: a throwaway POST verified the fabricated-ack path via the public entry before the real capture). RUNBOOK RULE: after any rollout, probe the entry path for the expected leg behavior BEFORE capturing (nacos/ribbon caches route to terminating pods for tens of seconds). ACK-TEXT NOTE: the flag-on fabricated msg ("create contacts success") differs from the flag-off/downstream persist msg ("Create Success") - a cross-leg textual differential tell (disclosed); within-leg success-shaped-clean. AS-DEPLOYED (rev-2.1 R2): trace-uninstrumented -> trace oracles not_applicable. PRE-REGISTERED DESIGN EXPECTATION (needs a traced capture): span-presence-visible under instrumentation -> tracetest_presence would flag the absent ts-contacts-service persist span (comparator also catches; not MIST-unique). G1-era 400 mystery RESOLVED: the old 400 came from the base image's routing/entity mismatch when requests were served by the base pod; the fork's addContact (edu.fudan.common.entity.Contacts, UUID ids) accepts the documented shape.
